dim_resolution.use: filter mc rows: keep iff cn_country_code[company_id-1] != 0 && != us_code

join_order.notes: cheapest probe first; small IN-set test on keyword_id
filter info_type_id == it2_id, then memcmp on info < '7.0'
filter info_type_id == it1_id, then info in {Germany,German,USA,American}; flat_hash_set<string_view>
two memmem calls on note (NOT LIKE %(USA)%, LIKE %(200%)%), then probe cn.country_code[company_id-1]; ct.id is no-op (4 ids); also track mc->company_id for projection of MIN(cn.name)

filters.predicate: note NOT LIKE '%(USA)%' AND note LIKE '%(200%)%'

data_structures.mi_info_set: flat_hash_set<string_view> with 4 literals; length-prefilter before compare
data_structures.cn_country_code_array: raw int16_t mmap of company_name/country_code.bin; probe by id-1
data_structures.offsets_indexes: mmap int32_t arrays for mk/mi/mi_idx/mc offsets_only on title.id
data_structures.aggregation: 3 scalar running mins (string_view) protected by per-thread locals then merged

parallelism.notes: Partition title id space [1..2528312] into morsels; each thread keeps local min for cn.name, mi_idx.info, t.title; merge at end. Dim resolution done single-threaded before driver.

projection.min_t_title: from title row v that passed all four EXISTS
projection.min_mi_idx_info: from any mi_idx row that satisfied the predicates for the surviving t
projection.min_cn_name: from cn.name[company_id-1] of any mc row that satisfied predicates for the surviving t

execution_notes: Order of per-title checks: (1) production_year>2008 (cheap int compare), (2) kt_ids.contains(kind_id), (3) mk EXISTS scan, (4) mi_idx EXISTS scan (track local mi_idx.info min for this title), (5) mi EXISTS scan, (6) mc EXISTS scan (track local cn.name min for this title via cn.country_code probe).
Only update global mins after all four EXISTS pass for the title; then also update MIN(t.title).
Short-circuit: as soon as any EXISTS fails for a title, skip remaining probes.
Per mc row: cheap predicates first — note memmem (NOT LIKE then LIKE; empty note fails LIKE), then cn.country_code dict probe.
Per mi_idx row: filter info_type_id == it2_id first, then memcmp info < '7.0'.
Per mi row: filter info_type_id == it1_id first, then IN-set check with length prefilter.
ct.id join is a no-op semantically (only need company_type_id non-NULL and in [1..4]); no explicit dim lookup required.
